correctness.rationale: Alternating host length 4k−1 covers every balanced binary target via greedy embedding and repeated-adjacent-pair bound. For k<=8, an exact prefix-completion DP tracks for each target the longest greedily embeddable prefix, branches over both appended bits and prunes only when current progress plus remaining host positions is below 2k. This necessary condition cannot remove a solution. Independent C implementation performed exhaustive full prefix-state enumeration at lengths 4k−2 and 4k−1 for k<=7, matching counts [2,10,44,190,800,3266,13018], palindromes and arch-index histograms; for k=8 length30 it searched 30,965,979 prefix nodes and found no host. Reversal/complement Burnside with odd host length gives orbit counts. Thus proof is a justified finite exhaustive computation, not extrapolation beyond k8.

Adamson covers hosts universal for ALL length-k words and gives the arch characterization; it does not count hosts for only complement-paired targets. Resultary contains broader binary subsequence-universality findings but no matching antisquare-restricted table in examined hits.
